variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model training is the repeated process of showing a model examples, measuring its error, and adjusting its parameters so it makes better predictions. A training run is more than a loop over data: it is a controlled experiment with a specific dataset, configuration, hardware environment, and evaluation rule.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Optimize
pairs.detail: Use batches to estimate error, backpropagate gradients, and update parameters.
pairs.explanation: Use batches to estimate error, backpropagate gradients, and update parameters. Lower training loss is evidence of fitting, not proof of usefulness.

pairs.label: Validate
pairs.detail: Measure held-out examples that were not used to choose updates.
pairs.explanation: Measure held-out examples that were not used to choose updates. Keep the split rule stable across comparable runs.

pairs.label: Recover
pairs.detail: Persist model weights, optimizer, scheduler, random state, and data position so an interruption resumes the same experiment.
pairs.explanation: Persist model weights, optimizer, scheduler, random state, and data position so an interruption resumes the same experiment.

variants.hint:
Optimize: Use batches to estimate error, backpropagate gradients, and update parameters.

Validate: Measure held-out examples that were not used to choose updates.

Recover: Persist model weights, optimizer, scheduler, random state, and data position so an interruption resumes the same experiment.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.explanation: Load batches, compute loss, update parameters, and checkpoint complete state at a recovery interval that fits the failure budget.

pairs.explanation: Promote only an explainable improvement. Stop divergence, data contract failures, and invalid evaluations before they consume the full budget.

pairs.label: Data parallel
pairs.detail: Replicate the model, split batches across workers, and synchronize gradients when one device can hold the state but throughput is too low.
pairs.explanation: Replicate the model, split batches across workers, and synchronize gradients when one device can hold the state but throughput is too low.

pairs.label: Model or state sharding
pairs.detail: Partition parameters, optimizer state, or activations when the model cannot fit on a single accelerator.
pairs.explanation: Partition parameters, optimizer state, or activations when the model cannot fit on a single accelerator. Measure communication before assuming linear speedup.

pairs.label: Federated learning
pairs.detail: Coordinate client updates when raw data must remain local.
pairs.explanation: Coordinate client updates when raw data must remain local. Non-identical client data and unreliable participation become first-class evaluation concerns.

pairs.label: Continual or active learning
pairs.detail: Use replay, retention tests, or targeted labeling when tasks change over time or labels are the scarce resource.
pairs.explanation: Use replay, retention tests, or targeted labeling when tasks change over time or labels are the scarce resource.

variants.prompt: What is the core promotion invariant for a training checkpoint?
options: It can be reproduced from versioned inputs and improves a protected validation measure
It has the lowest training loss from any run
It used the largest available accelerator
It completed without a worker restart
